So a split is noted by the exit that made it, and by every other trace live at that moment: while another tool holds the id, no exit's registration on it is complete, and a later complete registration needs a reclaim of that id (after its owner frees it), a re-take, or a rebinding to the other id, each of which appends to `_LOST`.

The silent shapes, all outside parties that undo their own change before a machinery step reads it: a party that cleared S sets it again itself; a party that replaced a callback restores it before any exit registers; a party that cleared a mint's local events sets them again before every holder's exit.

- **NOT_EXERCISED.** The fixed sentence reads: "work on other threads, pools, executors, child processes or asyncio tasks is credited only to a section that work opens itself; generator and coroutine objects created before the trace are never credited; a call counts only when it returns, yields or raises from inside its body while the tracer is active".

- (revision 9, GAP-18) Every metric and composition path is walked one key at a time: while the current value `x` has `issubclass(type(x), dict)`, the next is `dict.get(x, k, <sentinel>)`; a non-dict value or the sentinel ends the walk as "not present".
No `isinstance`, `in` or `[]` is applied to result data.
`score()` is not changed by this: it keeps v4's `_resolve` and v5e's `isinstance(_v, numbers.Real)` guard, and M11's only change to it is the `float()` OverflowError rule below.
Revision 9 (GAP-17) states the rule exactly: the note is "smoke run" iff smoke is truthy and `present` is false; in every other refusal it is `str(e)`, with the suffix iff smoke is truthy.
- **Spec-fixed texts (revision 9, GAP-15).** SM2's normalizer compares exactly these substrings of a message, and masks nothing else, so each is fixed byte for byte here.
Backticks elsewhere in this document are markup; none of these texts contains a backtick.
Placeholders render as follows, and nothing else in these substrings varies:
- `{T}`: a type's name, `_TYPE_QUAL.__get__(type(x))`, the `__qualname__` read through the C descriptor (so no metaclass property runs).
`the result has no 'coverage_trace' key`
Every one of these texts begins after the message's `[V5:CODE] ` prefix (and, for the scoring texts, after a `gate '<name>'` lead-in that is free-form).

For NOT_A_FUNCTION, FOREIGN_DEFINITION, INHERITED, INSTANCE_PATH and UNRESOLVED, SM2 compares the `module:qualname` the Resolution rules name (GAP-07's `<callee>`, GAP-25's defining class, Provenance (d)'s innermost function), rendered as those rules say, and nothing else of the text.

Where they land: at open, all before `_open`'s append (steps 1–5), so a hook that raises there propagates out of `run()` (or the coroutine's first step) before any append or store, and fn does not run (V71); in a callback, a raising hook makes that hit raise out of its callback (L-DELIVERY), and one raised at publication loses that one credit, inside I6; inside a transaction, they are further sites of the kind "Audit hooks and slow owners" and I5 describe, which the model's lock-taking and greenlet configurations stand for, and G_FI faults every instruction that makes them;
So revision 5 removed revision 4's two open- and close-path sites, `_txn()` in every clearing `_unwind_off` and `_alive` in every waiting open (the fifth critic's `critic5/c5_audit_events.py`).
The close path raises no audit event.
The open path raises audit events only before `_open`'s append: `_run`'s `sys._getframe()`, and step 5's `f_code` reads and `id()` calls.
`_commit` and everything after the append raise none.

sec: Invariants preserved by every prefix of every transition
text: After its core exits or is pruned, an opening holds no anchor, once its opener has left `_commit` (revision 4: an opener that stores after X3 or a prune detaches itself at step 8, and one that stored before is popped by X3 or the prune, which read the same `o.frame` key; the model check's END property, fault-free, on every pair and triple).
If `_TOOL[0]` was None, the next enter adopts the id and registers again (Tool acquisition; revision 8 self-audit, W7: X154e).
